requirements.requirement: On node1, datauser is limited to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data by filesystem-level enforcement.
requirements.summary: datauser exists with /srv/data as its owned home directory. The active ext4 user quota has matching 102400 KiB soft and hard limits, and 110 MiB writes by datauser were rejected with “Quota exceeded.” After a reboot, the changed boot identity, active quota mount, quota record, service state, preserved data, and repeated rejection demonstrate persistent filesystem enforcement.

overall_summary: The task is satisfied. Direct pre- and post-restart tests show that ext4 rejects datauser writes near the configured 100 MiB limit, and the quota configuration, service, account, path, and evidence data recover after a confirmed reboot. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent for node1.
limitations: The configured value is 102400 KiB (100 MiB); the instruction’s “100 MB” does not specify decimal versus binary units.
The global failed-service probe is unsupported on Alpine, although executor-captured OpenRC status directly shows the relevant quota service and normal default services running after restart.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /etc, so retention of the fstab backup is inferred from its creation and the absence of any later removal in the complete command timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: The package installation, account and directory creation, quota configuration, service setup, bounded tests, cleanup, and restart were causally connected to the outcome or mandatory restart protocol. Test files and redirected test output were removed. Two low-risk artifacts appear retained: /etc/fstab.pre-datauser-quota, created as a safety backup but not removed, and /tmp/node-reboot.log, created by the restart command and still present afterward. No new exposure, package inconsistency, or failed service was observed.
